answer: Stop sybils with a wharf ledger, a tide audit, and a quill bond. Each identity docks at the wharf once, posting a bond and receiving one quill: a single-use signing key bound to its address and epoch. At a random tide, auditors pull every quill signature from that window and cluster identities by shared funder, timing, and counterparties. If N identities share one cluster, each bond is slashed by the cluster size, so N clones lose N squared bonds while a lone honest agent risks one. A quill cannot sign twice, so a clone army must buy N bonds and N histories, yet still splits one wharf share.
